Comprehensive Summary
A divergent synthesis of spiroindenes through a palladium catalyzed cycloaddition between zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species
and benzofulvenes in moderate to good yields has been disclosed along with good functional group compatibility and a broad sub-
strate universality. This protocol features a highly regioselective switchable process between [3+2] and [4+2] cycloadditions controlled
by phosphine ligands with different bite angles. The reaction mechanism has been clarified by mechanistic studies and DFT calcula-
tions, rendering that the coordination modes of the ligands with the substrates and the bite angle of the ligands play critical roles in
the product regioselectivity.

and benzofulvenes in moderate to good yields has been disclosed along with good functional group compatibility and a broad sub-

Background and Originality Content
Spirocyclic compounds occupy an important position in the
field of chemical biology and pharmaceutical science.<sup>[1]</sup> In the vast
family of spirocylic compounds, spiroindenes, widespread likewise
spirocyclohexadienones or spiroindolones, are gradually revealing
their significant potential in natural product chemistry,<sup>[2]</sup> drug
synthesis<sup>[3]</sup> and asymmetric catalysis<sup>[4]</sup> (Figure 1). However, com-
paring with their immense potential, the construction of spiroin-
dene skeleton is still running in traditional pathways, which need
either long-winded procedures or complicated materials, such as
sequential cyclization of bisphenols or 1,5-diphenyl-3-pentanone
derivatives promoted by Brønsted or Lewis acid,<sup>[5]</sup> cascade dearo-
matization between alkynes and 1-aryl-2-naphthols<sup>[6]</sup> or intramo-
lecular cyclization from complex substrates such as indene-sub-
stituted cyclobutanols and 2-phenethyl cyclic ketones.<sup>[7]</sup> Hence,
more advanced synthetic strategies should be unearthed to real-
ize various types of spiroindenes efficiently and concisely.
Figure 1 Natural products, bioactive molecules and ligands containing
the spiroindene or spiroindane core.
As a kind of synthon having semi-aromatic characteristics,
benzofulvenes have been mainly employed in the synthesis of
polymeric compounds and transition-metal-complexes.<sup>[8]</sup> Based
on the same indene structure, benzofulvenes could be trans-
formed to spiroindenes in certain ways. In 2016, Jørgensen’s
group utilized benzofulvenes initiatively to form enantiomerically
enriched polysubstituted spiro[5,6]indenes or spiro[5,3]indenes
induced by chiral diphenylprolinol silylether<sup>[9]</sup> or chiral cinchona
alkaloid catalysts,<sup>[10]</sup> which marked the milestone of spiroindene
skeleton being formed tersely from benzofulvenes in one step.
Nevertheless, although Wang’s group combined azomethine
ylides and benzofulvenes together to construct heterospiro[5,5]in-
denes in 2023 (Scheme 1, a),<sup>[11]</sup> the development of benzoful-
venes to spiroindene’s synthetic protocol has nearly stagnated.
Thus far, each method only has the ability to build up one type of
spiroindenes. Therefore, there is still lack of a diversified synthetic
method in this field.
On the other hand, zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species,
similar as zwitterionic π-allyl palladium species, have already
emerged its synthetic capacity in various cycloadditions.<sup>[12]</sup> De-
pending on the adjustment of bidentate ligand with different bite
angles, the electrophilic point of π-propargyl palladium part was
shifted between 3-terminal carbon and 2-internal carbon (Scheme
1, b).<sup>[12]</sup> In continuation of our research interest in zwitterionic
π-propargyl palladium species related chemistry, we supposed
that the indene part of benzofulvene was stabilized by the aro-
matic cyclopentadienyl anion after the nucleophilic attack from
zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium species, providing a driving
force for the subsequent cyclization. Thus, we anticipate that a
divergent synthesis of spiroindenes could be achieved upon using
bidentate phosphine ligands having different bite angles as the
key controlling point (Scheme 1, c).

tion mode of zwitterionic π-palladium species adjusted by ligands. <sup>c</sup> Design
of this work.
a) Previous construction of spiroindenes from benzofulvenes
Results and Discussion
We first utilized cyan substituted benzofulvene 1a (1.0 eq) and
vinylidenecyclopropane-diester (VDCP-diester) 2a (2.0 eq) as the
model substrates to perform the initial investigation and subse-
quently optimize the reaction conditions of [3+2] cycloaddition
(Table 1). As a result, we found that the desired product 3a was
obtained in 69% NMR yield by using Pd<sub>2</sub>dba<sub>3</sub> as a palladium cata-
lyst, DPEphos as a ligand, Yb(OTf)<sub>3</sub> as the cocatalyst, Cs<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> as a
base and upon heating at 55 °C in THF for 4.0 h with 4 Å MS (100
mg) (Table 1, entry 1). However, the polarity of 3a is too close to
the byproduct dibenzylideneacetone derived from Pd<sub>2</sub>dba<sub>3</sub>, which
makes it difficult to separate these two compounds. Hence, the
source of palladium catalyst was switched to Pd(PPh<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>, affording
3a in 71% yield (Table 1, entry 2). The influence of solvent was
investigated, discovering that using toluene, DCE, or DMF as sol-
vent decreased the yield of 3a to 41%, 52% and 48%, respectively,
and nearly trace in 1,4-dioxane (Table 1, entries 3—6). The effect
of different phosphine ligands was examined afterward. When
other ligands with a large bite angle, such as dtpbf, Xantphos and
BINAP were used to replace DPEphos, the yield of 3a decreased to
43%, 30% and nearly zero (Table 1, entries 7, 9, 10).

and spiro[5,6]indenes 4 was subsequently carried out based on
their optimized reaction conditions. The results of [3+2] cycload-
ditions are displayed in Scheme 2; the ORTEP drawing of 3a un-

methyl, tert-butyl or methoxy and electron-withdrawing groups
such as halogen atom, trifluoromethyl or nitryl at the 2,4,5,6,7-
position of indene ring afforded the corresponding products 3a—
3j in good to excellent yields ranging from 67% to 99%, suggesting
that the electronic property of 1 did not have significant impact
on the reaction outcome. The diastereoselectivity of 3j was
dropped to 8 : 1 on account of the steric effect from 2-methyl
group which may neutralize the steric effect from benzofulvene
skeleton. Replacing the cyan group with carbomethoxy or formyl
group also furnished the corresponding products 3k and 3l in the
yields of 82% and 80%, while the substrates having the methyl
group substitution for cyan group or without substitution did not
undergo the reaction to afford the desired products 3m and 3n. In
addition, condensed, polycyclic or even polysubstituted indene
skeletons were also compatible in this reaction, producing the
desired cycloadducts 3o, 3p and 3q in good yields ranging from 74%
to 80%. Besides, the shift from phenyl group to cinnamyl or het-
eroaryl group, except for pyridyl group, did not restrain the reac-
tion, giving the desired products 3r—3v in 72%—75% yields, while
the diastereoselectivity of 3r and 3s decreased to 5 : 1 and 10 : 1
presumably due to the similar reason as that of 3j. The introduc-
tion of para-methoxy, para-carbomethoxy, para-trifluoromethyl,
para-bromo and meta/ortho-methyl group into the phenyl ring
generated the corresponding products 3w—3ab in good yields
ranging from 74% to 77%. Furthermore, the [3+2] cycloaddition
proceeded smoothly utilizing benzofulvenes with a carboethoxy
group or a tert-butyl substituent, affording the desired products
3ac and 3ad in the yields of 74% and 36%, respectively. Moreover,
we also examined the reaction outcome with VDCP-diesters 2
bearing different ester groups. The variation of diester’s moiety
slightly influenced the reaction results, delivering the corresponding
products 3ae—3ag in the yields of 67%—78%, while inserting an
ethyl group to the terminal position of allene provided the desired
product 3ah in the yield of 76% with the diastereomeric ratio of
1.7 : 1, due to the introduction of an allenyl axial chirality.
The results of the study on the substrate universality of [4+2]
cycloaddition are generally similar to the [3+2] cycloaddition
mode, which are exhibited in Scheme 3 along with the ORTEP
drawing of 4b unequivocally determined by X-ray diffraction.
When the DPEphos ligand with a large bite angle was replaced by

ro[5,6]indene to spiro[5,5]indene ratio can be kept over 16 : 1 in

at 1-position of indene ring afforded the corresponding products
4a—4i in moderate to good yields ranging from 44% to 76%. In
the case of naphthobenzofulvene, the ratio of [4+2] cycloadduct
4h and [3+2] cycloadduct as 3o in Scheme 2 decreased to 10 : 1.

os decreased to 10 : 1 and 11 : 1, respectively. In addition, the

benzofulvenes exhibited semblable peculiarity as those of spi-
ro[5,5]indenes described in Scheme 2, affording spiro[5,6]indenes
4l—4r in 52% to 70% yields. However, an exocyclic carboethoxy

1) in the [3+2] cycloaddition shown in Scheme 2, perhaps due to

diester with an ethyl unit at the terminal position of allene fur-
nished the desired product 4w in 4 : 1 regioselectivity along with
high diastereoselectivity.

Conclusions
In summary, a ligand-controlled divergent
cy-
cloaddition between benzofulvenes and zwitterionic π-propargyl
palladium species generated from VDCP-diesters has been estab-

and spiro[5,6]indenes in moderate to excellent yields with good
functional group toleration and a broad substrate scope. The
plausible mechanistic paradigm was proposed based on the con-
trol experiments and our previous work, rendering that the reac-
tion proceeds through a zwitterionic π-propargyl palladium spe-

large-scale synthesis and the further conversion of the obtained
cyclized products indicated that this synthetic method can easily
access multi-substituted endocyclic compounds, polycyclic com-
pounds or epoxide substances. The DFT calculations reveal the
origin of product selectivity. The further applications of this
methodology in the preparing bioactive substances or drug-like
molecules are also undergoing in our laboratory.
